the computation time for a simulation of the annual daylight penetration in a space is significantly reduced by using an adaptive time step, and by reducing the accuracy of the simulation by using an approximation of the sky model.

the following two adaptations of a radiosity algorithm bring down the required simulation time for an annual daylight simulation from the order of a day to the order of a few seconds: (1) The use of a simplified sky model that is based on a few representative sky conditions, and (2) the use of a simplified model of the solar radiation that is based on the average of all individual time-steps.

the computation time of an annual daylight simulation can be reduced from the order of hours to the order of minutes by using an algorithm that is based on the radiosity method, by using an algorithm for the computation of the sky component that is based on a ray-tracing algorithm, and by using a simplified sky model that is based on two sky types, the clear sky and the overcast sky.
